I am a microbiologist interested in evolvability—the ability of bacteria to adapt to changing environments and hosts.
Currently, I am a postdoc with [Astrid von Mentzer](https://www.gu.se/en/research/astrid-von-mentzer) at the University of Gothenburg in Sweden working on the evolution of the chaperone-usher pathway of gram-negative bacteria.
I completed my PhD in the [evolutionary microbiology group](https://www.ibe.upf-csic.es/evolutionary-microbiology-group) at ETH Zurich, Switzerland, in 2025.
In particular, I [explored](science/index.qmd#evolvability-of-bacteria-in-changing-environments) the upper limits of thermal adaptation of *Pseudoalteromonas haloplanktis* TAC125, an Antarctic marine bacterium, using experimental evolution, genomics and transcriptomics.

I enjoy coding and data visualisation, doing so primarily in R and from time to time Python.
I have written about some of my projects on my [blog](blog/index.qmd) and the source code can be found on [GitHub](https://github.com/gl-eb).

In my free time I like to observe and photograph birds.
I was first exposed to birding while growing up and dabbled in it on and off over the years, but only started birding more seriously in 2020.
My interest in photography also started out because of birds, though I have had landscape and sports photography phases.
You can see for yourself on [Flickr](https://www.flickr.com/photos/glebebert/).
